name: Kish
title: Saul's father and a Benjamite
summary: Kish was a wealthy man from the tribe of Benjamin and the father of Saul, Israel's first king. He is known as a prominent man of his clan, and his son was anointed by the prophet Samuel to become Israel's first king. Kish played an indirect but important role in Israel's transition from the period of the judges to the monarchy.

keyEvents.title: Kish's lineage
keyEvents.description: Kish is presented as the son of Abiel, a wealthy and prominent man from the tribe of Benjamin in Gibeah.

keyEvents.title: Kish's donkeys go missing
keyEvents.description: Kish's donkeys went astray, and he sent his son Saul out to look for them. This event led Saul to the prophet Samuel.

keyEvents.title: Saul is anointed king
keyEvents.description: When Saul went out to look for his father's donkeys, he met the prophet Samuel who anointed him as Israel's first king by God's command.

keyEvents.title: Saul Presented as King
keyEvents.description: Samuel gathered the people at Mizpah and presented Saul, son of Kish, as Israel's chosen king. Kish is specifically mentioned as his father's name in this royal selection.

keyEvents.title: Kish's Genealogy in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Kish's family tree and background are repeated in the books of Chronicles, where his connection to the tribe of Benjamin and his role as Saul's father are confirmed.

keyEvents.title: Paul Refers to Kish
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul mentions Kish in his speech at the synagogue in Antioch, stating that God gave the people Saul, son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin, as king for forty years.
